cases.name: Teri Lea Mathis Zenner
cases.about: She was a social worker for the Johnson County Mental Health Center and was working on her master's degree at the University of Kansas. "Teri was one of those people that once you met her, you would never forgot her," said Jennifer Jimerson, Lions softball head coach and one of Zenner's teammates. "She made a positive impact on everyone she knew." More than 1500 people attended her visitation.
cases.narrative:
He trapped Zenner in his bedroom. When his mother heard Zenner crying and threatened to call police, Zenner came stumbling out of the bedroom with a stab wound to the neck. He stabbed his mother repeatedly four times in the back, once in the chest, and once in the right arm and slashed her ear after she threw herself between her son and Teri. After his mother escaped to a neighbor's house, Ellmaker retrieved a chain saw from his bedroom and began cutting into her, almost severing her left forearm and her neck. He also slashed her head, back, and right hip.

After mutilating Teri, Andrew tried to commit suicide by ingesting a variety of pills. He then left the house with two pellet guns and attempted to drive away in Teri’s vehicle. When he had trouble getting the car to start, he took a can of gasoline from the garage, poured it on the vehicle, and set it on fire. As the police arrived, Andrew ran into the street. The police ordered him to drop his weapons, which he did. As Ellmaker was being handcuffed, he spontaneously stated, “I just killed my therapist with a chainsaw.”
